newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian markets stable, await Thai-IMF outcome.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian markets stable, await Thai-IMF outcome.

text.p: Indonesian financial markets were stable on Tuesday, extending their gradual rebound on the back of broad regional recoveries driven by prospects of an IMF rescue package for Thailand, dealers and brokers said.

Currency dealers said initial rises in the Thai baht, which rallied on brightened prospects of International Monetary Fund credit lines, dragged other Asian currencies up but the situation was reversed when the baht began to slip back.
However, the rupiah held on well, ending at 2,575/80 against the dollar in Jakarta after rising to a high of 2,560.

The rupiah opened at 2,575/85 against 2,585/95 at Monday's close. It had plunged to a historic low of 2,665 against the dollar last week after becoming the latest currency to fall victim to speculative attacks in the region.
The Jakarta stock market continued to recover on Tuesday, gaining 0.78 percent to close at 716.36, and remaining well supported above the psychologically important 700-point barrier.
But analysts said further stability of Indonesian financial markets would be determined by the outcome of Thailand's negotiations with the IMF on possible reform programmes.
They said fund managers were looking at the region as a whole at present and any negative news from the talks could drag the region into another wave of turbulence.

"A lot of people are still keeping a wait-and-see approach because basically most of the pressure on the currency seemed to be a Thai-contagion effect," a research director with a European brokerage house said.
"My viewpoint is that basically I don't think we are going to see stability in the markets probably for another couple of weeks because of currency volatility," he said.
However, some currency dealers said the rupiah was likely to recover gradually to 2,550 to the dollar by the end of the week on the back of offshore selling interest.
"You may get a considerable boost to the stock market, probably by the middle of next week, if the Thais agree to the IMF stability package," the brokerage director said.

Thai officials, admitting for the first time that they were ready to consider asking for an IMF loan, said on Monday they were in talks with a team from the fund to work out how to tackle the country's financial crisis and liquidity problems.
The crisis has already hurt economies in the region.
"The market probably will just sort of drift at the current level with no direction. Everyone will wait until next week to see what the position on Thailand will be," the director said.
"If there is no agreement on it, then it could be negative news. Until next week, until you see an indication for the IMF package, you are not going to see any stability in the markets."
A foreign brokerage analyst said he had not revised corporate earnings forecasts because of the uncertainty on the currency front.
He said, however, the pulp and paper sector could be one of the most affected because of large offshore borrowings.

"If the rupiah recovers slightly I think the index could go back to the 750 level by the end of the year which isn't a very dramatic rise from the present level," the analyst said, adding that there could be an impact on liquidity in the fourth quarter because of a slew of new public offerings.
